newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Taiwan futures off to slow, cautious start.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Taiwan futures off to slow, cautious start.

text.p: Taiwan stock index futures on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) kicked off to a slow and cautious start on Thursday, hamstrung by Taiwan regulators warning its investors not to trade, dealers said.

Taiwan has not yet legalised trading by local investors of the Taiwan stock index futures contracts launched on Wednesday by both SIMEX and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) on the Globex after-hours electronic trading system.
SIMEX began trade of its Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) Taiwan index at 0055 GMT, five minutes ahead of the CME's Dow Jones Taiwan stock index future.
On SIMEX, a mere 370 contracts changed hands in the first hour of trade, buoyed mostly by some commission house and local dealer orders, brokerage dealers said.
Locals are those who trade on their own account.
"The customer base is not there because of constraints on Taiwan investors," one foreign commission house dealer said.
"The simultaneous launch by Globex this morning has also affected liquidity," he added.
If not for the constraints, dealers said inaugural volume would have been healthier.
On Wednesday, Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission urged local investors not to engage in "illegal" trading of Taiwan futures in Singapore and Chicago.
It said the law prohibited local futures brokerages from placing orders for Taiwan investors through overseas affiliates, and violators would be punished.

Singapore dealers said Taiwan investors were not present in SIMEX and their absence could cripple trade in the contract, which opened at 299.7 points and climbed to a high of 311 points after the first hour.
The MSCI Taiwan index is a market-capitalisation-weighted index of 77 component stocks representing large, medium and small capitalised stocks covering 67 percent of Taiwan's stock market.
SIMEX said the index has an almost identical correlation with the Taiwan All Share Index (TAIEX) compiled by the Taiwan Stock Exchange. The contract will be cash settled.
Trade on the first day began at 0055 GMT and will end at 0415 GMT. Regular trading hours on weekdays will be 0045 to 0415 GMT, and 0845 to 1115 GMT on Saturday.
SIMEX chairman Victor Liew said the SIMEX contract was likely to do well as it would trade during Asian time on an open outcry system, as opposed to electronic trading on GLOBEX in Chicago.
He said SIMEX and CME had decided to launch separate contracts despite their long-standing tradition of cooperation as they had not been able to agree on several issues.
